title: Romans distinguish two special applications of promises (Jaubert)
source_text: XLI. Praeterea Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae non simpliciter & absolute negant fidelem posse & debere promissiones gratiae & salutis speciatim sibi applicare. Sed duplicem distinguunt promissionum divinarum specialem applicationem, sive appropriationem. Unam qua aliquis sic sibi appropriat, & ad se pertinere putat promissiones veris Dei filiis factas, quasi fide divina certus esset se de eo numero esse. Alteram, qua aliquis moraliter certus atque persuasus se esse Dei filium per gratiam ejus adoptatum, promissionibus divinis confidit, & earum erga se complementum expectat. Priorem illam applicationem damnant & rejiciunt, posteriorem vero probant & amplectuntur. Ut videre est apud eundem Jaubertum Archiepiscopum Arelatensem, Tom. 1. adversus Molinaei Clypeum, cap. 40. num. 9.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover the Doctors of the Roman Church do not simply and absolutely deny that a believer can and ought to apply the promises of grace and salvation specially to himself. But they distinguish a twofold special application, or appropriation, of the divine promises. One by which someone so appropriates to himself, and thinks to belong to himself, the promises made to the true sons of God, as if by divine faith he were certain he is of that number. The other, by which someone morally certain and persuaded that he is a son of God adopted by his grace, trusts the divine promises and expects their fulfillment toward himself. The former application they condemn and reject; the latter they approve and embrace. As may be seen in the same Jaubert, Archbishop of Arles, Tom. 1 against Molinaeus Shield, ch. 40 n. 9.
pass_b_english: Roman doctors do not simply deny special self-application of grace and salvation promises; they distinguish two appropriations.
Divine-faith certainty that one is already among God true sons they reject; moral certainty with trust expecting fulfillment they approve (Jaubert, Clypeus 1.40.9).

choices.why: Two appropriations: rejected divine-faith certainty vs approved moral trust.
